proposals_analyzed.title: SQLite Status Table
proposals_analyzed.proposed_schema: agent_status(agent_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, team TEXT, status TEXT, progress_pct REAL, current_task TEXT, blockers TEXT, findings_count INTEGER, output_files TEXT, last_updated REAL)
strengths: Atomic INSERT OR REPLACE eliminates all read-modify-write races that plague the per-agent JSON file approach
Single SELECT gives the coordinator a complete dashboard — no glob, no parse loop, no partial-read risks
SQLite WAL mode is already the established concurrency pattern in this codebase (help_protocol, direct_channels, work_stealing all use it)
Agents already have sqlite3 in stdlib — zero new dependencies
Schema is simple and purpose-built: one row per agent, always current
The coordinator already manages SQLite connections for help_protocol and direct_channels — adding one more table to the same DB is cheaper than managing a directory of JSON files

risks.risk: Redundancy with existing team_status table in help_protocol.py
risks.mitigation: Do NOT create a separate table. Extend the existing team_status table with the additional columns (agent_id, blockers, findings_count, output_files). This avoids two status systems competing for truth.

risks.risk: Redundancy with progress table in direct_channels.py
risks.mitigation: The progress table tracks phase-level progress per team. The hub status table tracks agent-level progress. They serve different granularities. Keep both but document that hub_status is the coordinator's primary read target.

risks.risk: SQLite busy contention when 8-10 agents write simultaneously
risks.mitigation: Already solved in this codebase. WAL mode + busy_timeout=30000ms + _retry_on_busy decorator handles this. The write is a single INSERT OR REPLACE — sub-millisecond lock hold time. Contention probability at 10 agents writing every 30s is negligible.
Coordinator checks last_updated and flags agents with stale timestamps. Same as the per-agent JSON approach but without the extra filesystem management.

risks.risk: Schema too flat — blockers and output_files as TEXT loses structure
risks.mitigation: Store blockers and output_files as JSON arrays in TEXT columns. SQLite has json_each() for queries if needed. Keep findings_count as INTEGER (summary stat) but add a key_findings TEXT column for the last 3-5 findings as a JSON array.

modifications: Use the EXISTING coordination SQLite database (same db_path as help_protocol, direct_channels, work_stealing) instead of creating a new DB or separate JSON files
Add agent-level granularity: the current team_status tracks teams, but the hub needs to track individual agents within teams
Add coordinator_instructions table as a sibling table for bidirectional communication
Add acknowledged_instructions column so agents can confirm receipt
Add started_at and estimated_completion columns for timeline tracking
Add requests_to_coordinator as a JSON TEXT column for agents to post structured requests

import json
import sqlite3
import time

def update_hub_status(db_path, agent_id, team, status, progress_pct, current_task,
                     subtasks_total=0, subtasks_done=0, blockers=None,
                     key_findings=None, findings_count=0, requests=None,
                     output_files=None, estimated_completion=None):
    """Write agent status to the hub. Called every 30s and on state changes."""
    now = time.time()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    conn.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000')
    conn.execute(
        '''INSERT INTO hub_agent_status
           (agent_id, team, status, progress_pct, current_task,
            subtasks_total, subtasks_done, blockers, key_findings,
            findings_count, requests, output_files, started_at, last_updated,
            estimated_completion)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
           ON CONFLICT(agent_id) DO UPDATE SET
            team=excluded.team, status=excluded.status,
            progress_pct=excluded.progress_pct,
            current_task=excluded.current_task,
            subtasks_total=excluded.subtasks_total,
            subtasks_done=excluded.subtasks_done,
            blockers=excluded.blockers,
            key_findings=excluded.key_findings,
            findings_count=excluded.findings_count,
            requests=excluded.requests,
            output_files=excluded.output_files,
            last_updated=excluded.last_updated,
            estimated_completion=excluded.estimated_completion''',
        (agent_id, team, status, progress_pct, current_task,
         subtasks_total, subtasks_done,
         json.dumps(blockers or []),
         json.dumps(key_findings or []),
         findings_count,
         json.dumps(requests or []),
         json.dumps(output_files or []),
         now, now,
         estimated_completion)
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()


def check_hub_instructions(db_path, agent_id):
    """Check for unacknowledged instructions from coordinator."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    conn.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000')
    rows = conn.execute(
        '''SELECT id, instruction_type, message, context, issued_at
           FROM hub_instructions
           WHERE target_agent_id = ? AND acknowledged_at IS NULL
           AND superseded_by IS NULL
           ORDER BY issued_at ASC''',
        (agent_id,)
    ).fetchall()
    instructions = [dict(r) for r in rows]
    conn.close()
    return instructions


def acknowledge_instruction(db_path, instruction_id, agent_id):
    """Acknowledge receipt of an instruction."""
    now = time.time()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    conn.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000')
    conn.execute(
        'UPDATE hub_instructions SET acknowledged_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND target_agent_id = ?',
        (now, instruction_id, agent_id)
    )
    # Also record in agent status
    conn.execute(
        '''UPDATE hub_agent_status
           SET acknowledged_instructions = json_insert(
               acknowledged_instructions, '$[#]', ?)
           WHERE agent_id = ?''',
        (instruction_id, agent_id)
    )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
implementation.coordinator_read_code:
import json
import sqlite3
import time

def read_hub_dashboard(db_path):
    """Read all agent statuses in one query. Returns list of dicts."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    rows = conn.execute(
        '''SELECT * FROM hub_agent_status
           ORDER BY
             CASE status
               WHEN 'blocked' THEN 0
               WHEN 'error' THEN 1
               WHEN 'waiting_for_instruction' THEN 2
               WHEN 'working' THEN 3
               WHEN 'starting' THEN 4
               WHEN 'idle' THEN 5
               WHEN 'complete' THEN 6
             END,
             progress_pct ASC'''
    ).fetchall()
    now = time.time()
    agents = []
    for r in rows:
        d = dict(r)
        d['blockers'] = json.loads(d['blockers'])
        d['key_findings'] = json.loads(d['key_findings'])
        d['requests'] = json.loads(d['requests'])
        d['output_files'] = json.loads(d['output_files'])
        d['age_seconds'] = now - d['last_updated']
        d['possibly_dead'] = d['age_seconds'] > 120
        agents.append(d)
    conn.close()
    return agents


def send_hub_instruction(db_path, target_agent_id, instruction_type, message, context=None):
    """Send an instruction to a specific agent."""
    now = time.time()
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    conn.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000')
    # Supersede any previous unacknowledged instruction of the same type
    cur = conn.execute(
        '''SELECT id FROM hub_instructions
           WHERE target_agent_id = ? AND instruction_type = ?
           AND acknowledged_at IS NULL AND superseded_by IS NULL''',
        (target_agent_id, instruction_type)
    ).fetchone()
    row_id = conn.execute(
        '''INSERT INTO hub_instructions
           (target_agent_id, instruction_type, message, context, issued_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)''',
        (target_agent_id, instruction_type, message,
         json.dumps(context or {}), now)
    ).lastrowid
    if cur:
        conn.execute(
            'UPDATE hub_instructions SET superseded_by = ? WHERE id = ?',
            (row_id, cur[0])
        )
    conn.commit()
    conn.close()
    return row_id


def get_blocked_agents(db_path):
    """Get agents that are blocked or have pending requests."""
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    rows = conn.execute(
        '''SELECT * FROM hub_agent_status
           WHERE status IN ('blocked', 'error', 'waiting_for_instruction')
           OR json_array_length(requests) > 0
           ORDER BY last_updated ASC'''
    ).fetchall()
    conn.close()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def get_stale_agents(db_path, stale_seconds=120):
    """Get agents whose last update is older than stale_seconds."""
    cutoff = time.time() - stale_seconds
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=30)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL')
    rows = conn.execute(
        '''SELECT * FROM hub_agent_status
           WHERE last_updated < ? AND status NOT IN ('complete', 'error')
           ORDER BY last_updated ASC''',
        (cutoff,)
    ).fetchall()
    conn.close()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def format_dashboard(agents):
    """Format agent status list into a readable table string."""
    if not agents:
        return 'No agents reporting.'
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"{'AGENT':<25} {'TEAM':<20} {'STATUS':<12} {'PROG':>5} {'TASK':<40} {'AGE':>6}")
    lines.append('-' * 112)
    for a in agents:
        flag = '!!' if a.get('possibly_dead') else ('**' if a['status'] in ('blocked','error') else '  ')
        task = (a.get('current_task') or '')[:38]
        age = f"{int(a.get('age_seconds', 0))}s"
        lines.append(
            f"{flag}{a['agent_id']:<23} {a['team']:<20} {a['status']:<12} {a['progress_pct']:>4.0f}% {task:<40} {age:>6}"
        )
    return '\n'.join(lines)
integration_points: Uses the same SQLite DB file as help_protocol.py, direct_channels.py, and work_stealing.py
Schema is initialized alongside existing schemas in coordinator_hub.py module init
agent_id in hub_agent_status corresponds to agent_id in help_protocol's work_items.agent_id
team in hub_agent_status corresponds to team in help_protocol's team_status.team
Coordinator reads hub_agent_status as primary dashboard, falls back to help_protocol.team_status for teams not yet reporting to hub

proposals_analyzed.title: Hub-and-Spoke Replacing Fire-and-Forget (NOT replacing agent-to-agent tools)
strengths: Correctly identifies the scope boundary: hub-spoke is for COORDINATOR VISIBILITY, not for replacing direct_channels or help_protocol peer communication
Addresses the root problem (coordinator flying blind) without disrupting working agent-to-agent patterns
Aligns perfectly with the layered architecture recommended in hub_spoke_analysis.json: Layer 1 (hub) for status, Layer 2 (direct_channels) for peer collab, Layer 3 (scratchpad) for data sharing
The existing tools (help_protocol, direct_channels, work_stealing) are battle-tested from TEAM-0022 through TEAM-0024 — no reason to disturb them
Makes the coordinator's role clear: it MONITORS via hub and STEERS via instructions. It does not relay data between agents.

risks.risk: Agents may use the hub instruction channel for data transfer instead of direct_channels/scratchpad
risks.mitigation: Document clearly: hub instructions are for DIRECTIVES (proceed, redirect, pause, abort, info, merge_with). Data sharing goes through scratchpad or direct_channels. Enforce a size limit on instruction message field (1024 chars).

risks.risk: Coordinator over-relies on hub and stops checking bus/help_protocol for urgent requests
risks.mitigation: The coordinator monitoring loop should read hub_agent_status FIRST (primary dashboard) then check help_protocol.get_open_help_requests() for any that haven't been surfaced through hub status requests. Belt and suspenders.

risks.risk: Confusion about which system to use when
risks.mitigation: Add a clear routing table to the SOP: 'Status updates -> hub. Help requests -> help_protocol. Peer data sharing -> scratchpad/direct_channels. Work distribution -> work_stealing queue.'

routing_table.coordinator_reassigns_work: help_protocol.auto_assign_idle_teams() triggered when hub shows idle agents + open help requests

coexistence_rules: ALL agents MUST write to hub_agent_status every 30 seconds. This is non-negotiable.
Agents MAY use direct_channels, help_protocol, work_stealing, and scratchpad as needed for peer coordination.
The hub is READ by the coordinator. The existing tools are USED by agents.
hub_instructions is the ONLY channel for coordinator-to-agent directives. Do not use the bus for this.
If an agent posts a help request via help_protocol, it MUST also set status='blocked' in hub so the coordinator sees it.

proposals_analyzed.title: Anti-Sequential Core Rule
proposals_analyzed.proposed_rule: Default to parallel. The burden of proof is on sequencing — you must justify WHY Task B can't start without Task A. Reading the same source code is not a dependency.
strengths: Directly attacks the most expensive anti-pattern observed in practice (TEAM-0024 coordinator initially planned sequential waves before being corrected)
The rule is crisp and memorable — a single sentence that can be embedded in every coordinator prompt
The litmus test is binary and actionable: 'Can B read the same source A reads? If yes, no dependency.'
Consistent with SOP-011 which already codifies this as ASR-001 through ASR-010
The hub-spoke visibility (PROP-001) is the enabler: the coordinator can now confidently run parallel because it can SEE and STEER in real-time
Historical evidence is strong: TEAM-0022 (18 agents, 1 wave), TEAM-0023 (20 agents, 1 wave), TEAM-0024 (8 agents, 1 wave) — all successful with maximum parallelism

risks.risk: Overzealous parallelism when true dependencies exist (e.g., Team B needs Team A's generated artifact)
risks.mitigation: The rule already has the escape hatch: 'you must justify WHY'. True dependencies like generated artifacts, trained models, or fetched external data are legitimate justifications. The key is that READING EXISTING CODE is never a justification.

risks.risk: File-write collisions when two agents edit the same file
risks.mitigation: This is a task assignment problem, not a parallelism problem. The coordinator must ensure file-disjoint task assignments. The anti-sequential rule applies to LAUNCH timing, not to file access patterns. Add to the rule: 'Conflict prevention is task isolation (different files), not temporal separation (different waves).'

risks.risk: Rule is ignored if not embedded in the right places
risks.mitigation: Embed the rule in THREE places: (1) coordinator system prompt, (2) SOP-011 pre-launch checklist, (3) a machine-readable guard in the launch code that counts launch waves and warns if >1.

modifications: Formalize the rule as a named constant that can be referenced: ANTI_SEQUENTIAL_RULE
Add a machine-checkable version: if the coordinator's launch plan has more than 1 wave, it must include a 'sequencing_justification' field per deferred team citing the specific artifact dependency
Pair the rule with the hub-spoke system: 'Default to parallel BECAUSE you have real-time visibility via the hub. If something goes wrong, you will see it and can intervene.'

implementation.rule_text: Default to parallel. The burden of proof is on sequencing. You must justify WHY Task B cannot start without Task A. Reading the same source code is NOT a dependency. Conflict prevention is through task isolation (different files), not temporal separation (different waves). You have real-time visibility via the hub — if something goes wrong, you will see it and intervene.

embedding_locations.how: Include the rule verbatim in the ANTI-PATTERNS section of the coordinator's instructions
Already partially there as ASR-001 through ASR-010. Consolidate into the single rule with the justification requirement.

A validate_launch_plan() function that takes the list of teams and their launch_wave number. If any team has wave > 0, it requires a 'sequencing_justification' string. Logs a warning if justification is missing.

launch_plan_schema.validation_rule: All teams should have launch_wave=0 unless depends_on_artifacts_from is non-empty AND the referenced artifact does not yet exist

proposals_analyzed.title: Single-Command Status Check
proposals_analyzed.proposed_mechanism: Each agent prompt includes instructions to write status to a designated path. The coordinator checks that path with one command instead of running 15 find commands.
strengths: Directly addresses the O(N) monitoring overhead where N is the number of agents
Reduces coordinator cognitive load: one action, full picture
Aligns with the SQLite approach in PROP-001 which gives this for free — a single SELECT is one command
Eliminates the current approach of running multiple 'find' or 'ls' commands across scattered output directories

risks.risk: If implemented as file-per-agent (the hub_spoke_analysis.json recommendation), the 'single command' is actually glob + N reads, which is still O(N)
risks.mitigation: This is precisely why PROP-001 (SQLite) is superior to per-agent JSON files. A single SQL query IS a single command regardless of agent count. The per-agent JSON approach still requires globbing and parsing N files.

risks.risk: Agents ignore the status-writing instruction in their prompt
risks.mitigation: Make the status update a CODE SNIPPET in the prompt, not a verbal instruction. Give agents a 3-line function call they copy-paste. Better: provide a hub_status_snippet.py that agents import.

risks.risk: Status path must be known at prompt-writing time
risks.mitigation: The DB path is a constant: storage/coordination/coordination.db. Include it as a literal in every agent prompt.

modifications: Merge with PROP-001: the 'single command' IS the SQLite SELECT. No separate implementation needed.

Provide a BASH one-liner for coordinators who want to check status without Python: sqlite3 storage/coordination/coordination.db 'SELECT agent_id, status, progress_pct, current_task FROM hub_agent_status ORDER BY progress_pct'

Provide a Python one-liner that can be embedded in coordinator prompts: python3 -c "import sqlite3,json; [print(f\"{r[0]:20} {r[2]:10} {r[3]:5.0f}% {r[4] or ''}\"[:80]) for r in sqlite3.connect('storage/coordination/coordination.db').execute('SELECT * FROM hub_agent_status ORDER BY progress_pct')]"
For maximum simplicity, provide a hub_dashboard.py CLI script that the coordinator calls with one bash command

implementation.integration_with_prop_001: PROP-004 is fully subsumed by PROP-001. The SQLite table IS the single status path. The dashboard script IS the single command. No separate implementation needed.

synergies: PROP-001 (SQLite) + PROP-004 (single command) are two facets of the same solution. SQLite gives atomicity; the dashboard query gives single-command access.
PROP-002 (scope boundary) + PROP-001 (SQLite) coexist cleanly because the hub tables live in the same DB as help_protocol/direct_channels. One DB, multiple coordination layers.

PROP-003 (anti-sequential) + PROP-001 (hub visibility) are mutually reinforcing: the hub gives the coordinator confidence to run parallel, and parallel execution is the whole point of the anti-sequential rule.
conflicts: PROP-001 (SQLite) conflicts with the hub_spoke_analysis.json recommendation of per-agent JSON files. Resolution: SQLite wins. The analysis itself noted SQLite as 'viable' and only rejected it as 'overkill'. But the analysis underestimated the value of atomic writes and single-query dashboard. With the existing codebase already using SQLite for 3 other coordination modules, adding one more table is less overhead than managing a directory of JSON files.
PROP-004 originally assumed file-based status. With PROP-001 providing SQLite, PROP-004 simplifies to 'write a dashboard CLI script'.
cross_proposal_analysis.resolution: The hub_spoke_analysis.json's per-agent JSON file approach is architecturally clean but pragmatically inferior to SQLite in this specific codebase where SQLite is already the established pattern. The JSON approach requires: (1) directory management, (2) glob + parse loop, (3) temp-file-then-rename for atomicity, (4) no query capability. SQLite requires: (1) one INSERT OR REPLACE, (2) one SELECT, (3) built-in atomicity, (4) full query capability for filtering/sorting. The coding team should implement SQLite.

classes.name: HubAgent
classes.purpose: Agent-side interface. Each agent creates one instance and uses it to post status and check instructions.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Open SQLite connection with WAL mode, create tables if not exist, record started_at timestamp

methods.name: update_status
methods.description: INSERT OR REPLACE into hub_agent_status. Validates status against enum. JSON-encodes list fields. Uses _retry_on_busy decorator.

methods.name: check_instructions
methods.description: SELECT from hub_instructions WHERE target_agent_id = self.agent_id AND acknowledged_at IS NULL AND superseded_by IS NULL. Returns list of instruction dicts.

methods.name: acknowledge
methods.description: UPDATE hub_instructions SET acknowledged_at = now WHERE id = instruction_id. Also appends to acknowledged_instructions JSON array in hub_agent_status.

classes.name: HubCoordinator
classes.purpose: Coordinator-side interface. The coordinator creates one instance and uses it for monitoring and steering.

methods.name: __init__
methods.description: Open SQLite connection with WAL mode, create tables if not exist

methods.name: dashboard
methods.description: SELECT * FROM hub_agent_status ORDER BY status priority (blocked first, complete last), then progress_pct ASC. Decorates each row with age_seconds and possibly_dead flag (>120s stale).

methods.name: get_team_summary
methods.description: Aggregate agent statuses by team. Returns {team: {agents: N, avg_progress: float, blocked_count: int, complete_count: int, min_progress: float}}.

methods.name: send_instruction
methods.description: INSERT into hub_instructions. If a previous unacknowledged instruction of the same type exists, set its superseded_by to the new row ID.

methods.name: broadcast_instruction
methods.description: Send the same instruction to all agents in a team. Queries hub_agent_status for agents with matching team, then calls send_instruction for each.

methods.name: get_blocked_agents
methods.description: SELECT agents with status in (blocked, error, waiting_for_instruction) or json_array_length(requests) > 0.

methods.name: get_stale_agents
methods.description: SELECT agents with last_updated < now - stale_seconds AND status NOT IN (complete, error).

methods.name: get_unacknowledged_instructions
methods.description: SELECT from hub_instructions WHERE acknowledged_at IS NULL AND superseded_by IS NULL. Useful for detecting agents that aren't reading instructions.

methods.name: format_dashboard
methods.description: Format agent list as a human-readable table with columns: agent_id, team, status, progress, task, age. Highlight blocked/error/stale rows.

standalone_functions.name: update_hub_status
standalone_functions.purpose: Standalone function for agents that can't import the class (e.g., bash-embedded Python one-liners). Opens connection, writes, closes. Stateless.

standalone_functions.name: check_hub_instructions
standalone_functions.purpose: Standalone function for agents to check instructions without maintaining a persistent connection.

standalone_functions.name: validate_launch_plan
standalone_functions.purpose: Validates a coordinator's launch plan against the anti-sequential rule. Returns list of warnings.
standalone_functions.rule: All teams should have launch_wave=0 unless depends_on_artifacts_from references a non-existent artifact

cli_tool.usage: python3 hub_dashboard.py [--db PATH] [--format table|json] [--blocked-only] [--stale N] [--team TEAM]
cli_tool.description: CLI tool for coordinator to check agent status. Default output is a formatted table. --format json for machine-readable output.
cli_tool.implementation_note: Uses argparse. Imports HubCoordinator. Calls dashboard() and format_dashboard(). Exits with code 1 if any agent is blocked or stale (useful for scripted monitoring).

agent_integration.prompt_template_addition:
## STATUS REPORTING (MANDATORY)
You MUST report your status to the coordination hub. Use this code:

```python
import sqlite3, time, json
def hub_status(agent_id, team, status, pct, task, **kw):
    c = sqlite3.connect('storage/coordination/coordination.db', timeout=30)
    c.execute('PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL'); c.execute('PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000')
    c.execute('''INSERT INTO hub_agent_status (agent_id,team,status,progress_pct,current_task,started_at,last_updated)
        VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?) ON CONFLICT(agent_id) DO UPDATE SET
        status=excluded.status,progress_pct=excluded.progress_pct,
        current_task=excluded.current_task,last_updated=excluded.last_updated''',
        (agent_id,team,status,pct,task,time.time(),time.time()))
    c.commit(); c.close()
```

Call `hub_status('YOUR_AGENT_ID', 'YOUR_TEAM', 'working', PROGRESS_PCT, 'description of current task')` at:
- Task start (status='working', pct=0)
- After each subtask completion (update pct)
- When blocked (status='blocked')
- When complete (status='complete', pct=100)
- At minimum every 30 seconds
agent_integration.frequency: Every 30 seconds minimum. After every significant state change (task start, subtask complete, blocker, completion).
agent_integration.schema_bootstrap: The HubAgent.__init__ and the standalone update_hub_status function both CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so the first agent to write bootstraps the schema. No pre-setup needed.

coordinator_integration.monitoring_loop:
The coordinator's monitoring cycle becomes:
1. agents = hub.dashboard()  # single query, full picture
2. blocked = [a for a in agents if a['status'] in ('blocked','error') or a['possibly_dead']]
3. If blocked: send_instruction() to redirect or provide info
4. stale = [a for a in agents if a['possibly_dead']]
5. If stale: log warning, consider relaunching
6. Check help_protocol.get_open_help_requests() for requests not surfaced via hub
7. If idle agents exist and help requests are open: help_protocol.auto_assign_idle_teams()
8. Print format_dashboard(agents) for human visibility
coordinator_integration.polling_interval: 10-15 seconds between dashboard checks. The coordinator reads the dashboard as part of its natural conversation loop (e.g., between checking on completed agents).
coordinator_integration.integration_with_sop_011: SOP-011's monitoring_protocol section should be updated to reference hub_dashboard as the primary monitoring tool instead of multiple find commands and bus reads.

edge_cases.db_not_created_yet: Both HubAgent and HubCoordinator run CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on init. First write bootstraps everything. Coordinator calling dashboard() on empty table returns empty list — no error.
edge_cases.agent_crashes_mid_write: SQLite WAL mode ensures the write either completes or doesn't. Partial writes are not visible. The agent's last valid status remains in the table.
edge_cases.two_agents_same_id: agent_id is PRIMARY KEY. Second agent's INSERT OR REPLACE overwrites the first. This is a configuration error — agent IDs must be unique. The coordinator should detect duplicates by checking for suspiciously rapid last_updated changes.
edge_cases.coordinator_crashes: Agent status rows persist in SQLite. Next coordinator session reads them. Instructions already sent persist. Agents may have acknowledged instructions the coordinator doesn't know about — but acknowledged_at timestamps are in the DB for recovery.
edge_cases.db_locked_for_extended_period: busy_timeout=30000ms (30 seconds) handles normal contention. _retry_on_busy with exponential backoff handles extreme cases. If the DB is locked for >30s, something is fundamentally wrong (disk failure, hung process) — the retry will surface the error.
edge_cases.very_large_number_of_agents: The hub is designed for 3-20 agents. At 100+ agents, the single SQLite DB may become a bottleneck on writes. For this system's use case (6-10 teams, 8-20 agents), SQLite handles it trivially.
edge_cases.instruction_not_read: Coordinator can query get_unacknowledged_instructions() to detect agents ignoring instructions. If an instruction is unacknowledged for >60s and the agent's last_updated is recent, the agent is not checking. Coordinator can re-send with 'abort' type as escalation.
edge_cases.superseded_instructions: If the coordinator sends 'redirect' then quickly sends another 'redirect' before the first is acknowledged, the first is marked superseded_by the second. Agent only sees the latest. No instruction queue buildup.

anti_sequential_integration.rule_constant: ANTI_SEQUENTIAL_RULE = 'Default to parallel. The burden of proof is on sequencing. You must justify WHY Task B cannot start without Task A. Reading the same source code is NOT a dependency. Conflict prevention is through task isolation (different files), not temporal separation (different waves). You have real-time visibility via the hub — if something goes wrong, you will see it and intervene.'
anti_sequential_integration.enforcement: Coordinator calls validate_launch_plan() before launching. Warnings are printed. Launch is NOT blocked (coordinator has final authority) but warnings create an audit trail.
